title: Horse Wrestling and Hegemony: Why Central Asia's Nomad Games Matter This Year | Council on Foreign Relations
gist: The World Nomad Games and SCO summit in Bishkek showcase Central Asia's dual role as an economic 'lifejacket' for sanctioned Iran and Russia and a potential energy-market winner as Kazakh oil and Turkmen gas gain relative appeal amid Strait of Hormuz disruption, while China's 'no-limits' partnership with Russia has shifted from peer alliance to client relationship.

themes.theme: Central Asia as economic lifejacket for Iran and Russia

insights.claim: With US sanctions crippling Iran's economy and a naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz significantly reducing its oil exports, Iran is finding limited economic relief through deepened trade with Central Asian neighbors, part of a long-term pivot strategy that predates but is being accelerated by the ongoing war.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Central Asian trade routes are becoming a measurable sanctions-evasion release valve for Iran — a factor that could partially blunt the economic effectiveness of the Hormuz blockade over time.

insights.claim: Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, as Eurasian Economic Union members alongside Russia, enable transfer of Western electronics, microchips, and machine tools without customs scrutiny; EU trade data shows imports of high-priority dual-use items from Europe into Kyrgyzstan ran 800 percent above pre-invasion levels in the first ten months of 2025, while Kyrgyz exports of those same items to Russia were 1,200 percent higher.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: These specific percentage increases (800%/1,200%) are hard, trackable evidence of a live sanctions-evasion corridor for dual-use goods reaching Russia's war effort — a concrete target for tightened Western export-control enforcement.
insights.locator: Body paragraph on Russia and sanctions evasion

insights.claim: For both Iran and Russia, Central Asia functions as a 'lifejacket' — it will not rescue them from their current crises but will sustain them through stormy geopolitical times, while China plays the more durable role of 'lifeboat' for both, having turned its partnership with Russia from one of peers into a clientelist relationship and openly serving as de facto benefactor and protector for Iran.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: The lifejacket/lifeboat framework is a useful mental model for weighting the relative durability of sanctioned states' economic support networks — Central Asian relief is marginal and temporary, Chinese backing is structural and durable.

insights.claim: Days before the SCO summit, China stressed it would not have the terms of its engagement with Iran, its de facto client state, dictated by the United States, explicitly denouncing and dismissing the threat implicit in what the author calls 'Economic D-Day' (secondary sanctions); China is the one country that could plausibly deliver Iran to the negotiating table but has shown no interest in doing so.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: China's explicit refusal to leverage its Iran relationship for US diplomatic goals signals that secondary-sanctions threats against Chinese entities trading with Iran are unlikely to change Beijing's calculus in the near term.
insights.locator: Body paragraph on China and Iran

themes.theme: Energy market implications of Central Asian resource wealth

insights.claim: Kazakhstan produces nearly as much oil as Kuwait and is already a significant supplier to the EU, while Turkmenistan holds the world's fourth-largest natural gas reserves and sells almost all of it to China — positioning both as increasingly attractive energy suppliers as global buyers seek to de-risk away from Strait of Hormuz instability.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Kazakh oil and Turkmen gas are direct beneficiaries of Hormuz-driven energy de-risking, making Central Asian energy exporters worth watching as relative winners of Middle East instability even without new production growth.

insights.claim: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization has shown staying power in bolstering regional ties even though its broader geopolitical impact as a counterweight to Western blocs has been exaggerated, and the sixth World Nomad Games was grander than ever before — evidence that regionalism grounded in shared geography and culture is becoming a defining feature of global politics as stability increasingly comes from concentrated alliance networks rather than diffused global economic integration.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: The SCO/Nomad Games convergence is offered as a leading indicator of a broader global shift from diffuse globalization toward 'coalitions of the willing' — relevant context for assessing the durability of Western-led multilateral institutions relative to regional blocs.
insights.locator: Later section on fragmentation and globalization

insights.claim: Xi Jinping was expected to attend the SCO summit's opening ceremony but pulled out to focus on the response to disastrous flooding and landslides in Tibet, while Putin, Modi, and Pezeshkian all attended in person alongside other SCO heads of state.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: Xi's absence from a marquee SCO event to manage a domestic disaster is a small but notable signal of competing domestic priorities even as China deepens its geopolitical leadership role in Central Asia.

themes.theme: Other macro developments flagged in passing

insights.claim: US government debt tipped over the $40 trillion mark in the weeks preceding this piece, sending bond yields to their highest level since 2008, mentioned alongside a pause-and-resume of US military operations against Iran and collapsed US-Canada trade talks as evidence of an unusually eventful August.
insights.speaker: Michael Froman
insights.so_what: The $40 trillion debt threshold and 2008-level bond yields are a significant standalone macro data point flagged even in a piece nominally about Central Asian games — a reminder that fiscal/rates stress is running in parallel with the geopolitical narrative.
